alternate_names: Shri Bhagwan Bahubali Digambar Jain Statue
deities: Bahubali (Gommateshwara) - the 39-ft monolithic statue; in Jainism Bahubali is revered as a liberated soul (Siddha), son of the first tirthankara Rishabhanatha
festivals: Mahamastakabhisheka - the grand head-anointing ceremony held once every 12 years; at Dharmasthala it has been performed in 1982, 1995, 2007 and 2019

history.dynasty: Modern-era monument; commissioned under the aegis of the Jain Heggade family of Dharmasthala (Dharmadhikaris), not a historical dynasty
history.period: Sculpted 1967-1973 by Renjala Gopalkrishna Shenoy under the aegis of Shri Ratnavarma Heggade; transported from Karkala in 1970; installed atop Ratnagiri Hill in February 1982 by Dr. D. Veerendra Heggade
history.summary: THIS IS A JAIN MONUMENT (39-ft monolithic statue), NOT A HINDU TEMPLE - keep-or-drop decision needed for this temple CSV row. The Bahubali (Gommateshwara) statue stands atop Ratnagiri Hill about 1 km from the Manjunatha temple at Dharmasthala, Dakshina Kannada. The dream of a Bahubali monolith at Dharmasthala was envisioned by the late Shri Ratnavarma Heggade and late Maatrushree Rathnamma Heggade; sculptor Renjala Gopalkrishna Shenoy carved the 39-ft statue over 1967-1973 from a monolithic stone at Mangalapaade, Karkala (64 km away). In 1970 the 170-tonne (some accounts say 180-tonne) statue with its 13-ft pedestal was hauled 64 km on a 64-wheel trolley pulled by three 250-HP tractors over winding ghat roads, and it was positioned atop Ratnagiri Hill in February 1982 by Dr. D. Veerendra Heggade, who had become Dharmadhikari at age 20. The Digambara-form monolith symbolises renunciation, self-control and subjugation of the ego as the first step to salvation; Bahubali is the son of the first Jain tirthankara Rishabhanatha (Adinath), who renounced his kingdom to his brother Bharata and attained enlightenment through penance. The Mahamastakabhisheka of the Dharmasthala statue has been performed four times since installation: 1982, 1995, 2007 and 2019. It is the third of the five Bahubali monoliths of Karnataka over 20 ft tall (Shravanabelagola 57 ft, Karkala 42 ft, Dharmasthala 39 ft, Venur 35 ft, Gommatagiri 20 ft).

name: Bahubali (Gommateshwara) Statue Shrine
town: Dharmasthala (CSV town 'Dharmasthala' is correct; the statue is atop Ratnagiri Hill, about 1 km from the Manjunatha temple, in Belthangadi taluk)
town_description: Dharmasthala is a famous pilgrimage town in Belthangadi taluk of Dakshina Kannada district, Karnataka, about 75 km from Mangalore. Centred on the 800-year-old Sri Manjunatha Swamy temple administered by the Jain Heggade family, it also hosts the 39-ft Bahubali monolith atop nearby Ratnagiri Hill, whose Mahamastakabhisheka is held every 12 years and draws Jain pilgrims from across the country.
tradition: Jainism (Digambara) - NOT a Hindu temple; Bahubali is a revered Siddha in Jain hagiography

travel.road: The hilltop shrine is about 1 km from the Manjunatha temple; reachable by climbing steps for about 20 minutes (about 200 steps per one visitor account) or by road; autos available at the entrance (verify).

visitor_information.best_time: Visit in the morning to avoid humidity and sunny weather; October to March is the best season.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Reportedly open 8:00 AM - 10:00 AM and 6:00 PM - 7:00 PM daily (verify - from one travel source only). Shelter and drinking water are available on the hilltop; the hilltop gives a view over the temple town of Dharmasthala.
